original_claim: Parallelising the integration-test groups will reduce CI elapsed time by at least 40% without changing test outcomes.

current_claim.text: The supplied workflow description identifies a candidate for a controlled parallelisation trial; it does not establish a 40% reduction or preservation of test outcomes.
current_claim.qualifier: Unsupported performance prediction. The only supplied record is a synthetic description.

stronger_target.text: For the frozen runner configuration and representative test revisions, parallel test groups reduce median CI elapsed time by at least 40%, while preserving the preregistered outcome and isolation criteria.
stronger_target.qualifier: Conditional target requiring paired measurements, declared uncertainty and independent isolation checks.

scope.system_boundary: Integration-test execution stage, including fixture setup and teardown.
scope.configuration: Linux runner and four test groups; exact runner size, revision and database configuration remain to be frozen.
scope.operating_conditions: Representative revisions, runner contention and cache states must be sampled and recorded.
scope.units: Elapsed time in seconds and paired relative reduction as a percentage.
scope.time_horizon: The planned trial and identified repository revisions only.
scope.consequences: Faster feedback is valuable only when test coverage and outcome reliability remain acceptable.

grounds.statement: The synthetic workflow description reports sequential groups and a possible shared fixture database.
The parallel configuration achieves the specified timing and outcome criteria under representative conditions.

warrants.rule: An explicit supplied description supports a bounded report of what that description says.
warrants.applicability: Applies only to the supplied synthetic text and does not establish actual production behaviour.

warrants.rule: A sequential workflow identifies a candidate for a controlled scheduling trial when interference and representativeness are investigated.
warrants.applicability: Supports planning the trial only. No quantitative benefit follows from sequential scheduling alone.

warrants.rule: Paired measurements on frozen, representative revisions can support a bounded performance comparison when outcome preservation and interference are checked separately.
warrants.applicability: Requires representative sampling and explicit treatment of cache state, fixture overhead and runner contention. The warrant remains a proposed methodological justification.

assumptions.statement: The test groups can execute concurrently without sharing mutable state that changes their outcomes.
assumptions.validation: Inspect fixture ownership and run isolation and order-perturbation checks before relying on timing results.

defeaters.challenge: A timing improvement could arise from different cache or runner conditions rather than the scheduling change.
defeaters.response: Counterbalance run order and record cache state and contention in paired runs.

defeaters.challenge: Shared fixture mutations could alter test outcomes under concurrent execution.
defeaters.response: Investigate through the isolation checks for A1. This possibility is not an observed failure.

alternatives.explanation: Fixture setup or CPU contention may dominate elapsed time, leaving little benefit from parallel group scheduling.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Measure group, fixture and runner-resource timings in both configurations on the same revisions.

evidence_plan.question: Does the identified parallel configuration meet the timing and outcome criteria?
evidence_plan.method: Freeze revisions and runner configuration. Pilot the variance, then preregister a paired, counterbalanced trial with sample size chosen from that pilot. Retain complete timing and outcome records.
evidence_plan.comparator: The existing sequential workflow on the same revisions and runner configuration.
evidence_plan.acceptance_criterion: The preregistered interval for median relative reduction must support at least 40%. Outcome preservation must pass separately declared coverage, isolation and repeated-run criteria.
evidence_plan.if_failed: Reject the 40% target or narrow it to the revisions and conditions actually supported by the observations.
evidence_plan.cost: CI runner time and analysis effort, to be estimated from the pilot.
evidence_plan.measurement: Elapsed time in seconds, relative reduction in percent, and recorded outcome/isolation failures as counts.

evidence_plan.question: Do concurrent groups interfere through shared mutable fixtures?
evidence_plan.method: Inspect fixture ownership, allocate isolated resources where necessary, perturb scheduling and repeat the same tests under sequential and parallel execution.
evidence_plan.comparator: Sequential execution and an isolated-fixture parallel configuration.
evidence_plan.acceptance_criterion: No demonstrated cross-group state interference in the declared checks, with remaining coverage limits reported. Passing finite tests supports only the tested conditions.
evidence_plan.if_failed: Repair isolation or retain sequential execution for the affected groups.
evidence_plan.cost: Fixture engineering and repeated test execution.
evidence_plan.measurement: Recorded fixture interference and outcome discrepancies as counts.

evidence_plan.question: Could cache state or runner contention explain the timing difference?
evidence_plan.method: Counterbalance configuration order, stratify cache state and log runner-resource contention in the paired trial.
evidence_plan.comparator: Both configurations within each recorded cache and contention condition.
evidence_plan.acceptance_criterion: The claimed reduction must survive the preregistered condition checks or be explicitly restricted to supported conditions.
evidence_plan.if_failed: Restrict the claim or repeat the study with better control of the identified confounder.
evidence_plan.measurement: Cache-state categories, runner contention measures and elapsed time in seconds.

evidence_plan.question: Does shared fixture mutation change outcomes under concurrent execution?
evidence_plan.method: Use the fixture inspection and scheduling perturbation checks specified for A1, retaining individual outcome records.
evidence_plan.measurement: Cross-group state interference and outcome discrepancies as counts, with revision and scheduling identifiers.
evidence_plan.comparator: Sequential execution and isolated-fixture parallel execution on the same revisions.
evidence_plan.acceptance_criterion: No demonstrated cross-group interference in the preregistered checks, with finite coverage limits retained.
evidence_plan.if_failed: Retain sequential scheduling for affected groups or repair fixture isolation before making the stronger claim.
evidence_plan.cost: Shared with the A1 isolation investigation.

residual_risks: Finite trials may miss rare interference or timing conditions.
The synthetic record supplies no empirical performance evidence.
decision_limits: Use this example to plan a trial. It supplies no production performance or correctness assurance.
Agent agreement and successful schema validation do not establish the truth of the claim.
adjudication: The 40% claim exceeds the supplied support. Retain it as a testable target, prioritise fixture isolation and paired measurements, and reassess against the retained observations.

subclaims.text: The supplied synthetic description identifies sequential test execution and possible fixture sharing.
subclaims.qualifier: A report of the supplied description only, with no production measurements.

compositions.rationale: The bounded description claim relies on the source-report warrant W1.
The present conclusion relies on W2, which connects the source description to a proposed controlled trial.
The stronger target requires both the descriptive subclaim and the missing comparative measurements within W3. Its premises are jointly required.

reading.title: The description justifies planning a trial

paragraphs.text: The supplied description identifies a candidate for a controlled parallelisation trial. It provides no empirical basis for predicting a 40% reduction or for claiming that test outcomes will be preserved.

The synthetic workflow description reports four integration-test groups running in sequence and possible sharing of a fixture database. These details establish what the example says about its workflow, while leaving actual production timing and interference unmeasured.

Sequential scheduling gives a reason to investigate concurrent execution because some work may overlap. The practical warrant therefore supports a trial decision, while the stronger performance claim requires the comparative measurements represented by G2.

The proposed trial must test whether mutable fixtures change outcomes when groups overlap. Cache state and runner contention also need control because they could explain a timing difference independently of the scheduling change. The isolation and counterbalanced measurement plans address these unresolved conditions.

The immediate next step is to freeze the runner configuration and investigate isolation before running the paired timing trial. Retain the 40% improvement as a conditional target, then narrow or reject it if the recorded observations fail its declared criteria.

The supplied synthetic description reports sequential integration-test groups and possible fixture sharing. This subclaim concerns the contents of that record and carries no production performance result.

That bounded finding follows through W1 from the explicit report G1. It can inform the design of an investigation, with the excerpt retained so a reviewer can inspect the source of the interpretation.

The stronger target asks whether a specified parallel configuration achieves at least a 40% median reduction while meeting separately declared outcome and isolation criteria. It remains conditional because the comparative measurements are missing.

A paired, counterbalanced trial can supply evidence for that bounded comparison after fixture interference has been investigated. Passing the stated criteria would justify reassessing the target within the tested configuration, with residual uncertainty retained.
